mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average compresses equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without regime restrictions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns show no positive correlation with FEDFUNDS levels in any 3-year rolling window (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0 percent, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending confidence, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in consumer spending (RSAFS) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust economic momentum, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through improved corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising RSAFS and rising INDPRO fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During active monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising at least 0.5% over 3 months), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced liquidity and higher discount rates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods classified as monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising >0.5% in 3 months).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without regime restrictions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns show no positive correlation with PAYEMS growth rates in any 3-year rolling window (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 2000 thousand units, it signals a contraction in the housing sector that reduces consumer wealth and business investment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST < 2000 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate a dual stress of monetary tightening and economic slowdown, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising FEDFUNDS and rising UNRATE fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During industrial slowdowns (INDPRO below 95.0 index value), manufacturing output contraction reduces corporate earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where INDPRO < 95.0.
